answer: Each agent must post a bond that is locked before it can submit work, and the bond is forfeited if a randomly selected audit finds fabricated activity. This makes identity creation costly: an attacker must fund many separate bonds and keep them tied up while building history, rather than minting free accounts. A reputation signal can grow with verified work, but splitting one history across aliases does not multiply trust. The lotus test is whether audits catch coordinated accounts; a successful fraud can trigger a ripple of losses across every bonded identity.
